tips.accordion.cash.title: Cash & ATMs
tips.accordion.cash.body: Many places prefer cash. There's no ATM in town — withdraw in Zihuatanejo or Troncones before you arrive, and keep small bills for tacos and taxis.
tips.accordion.signal.title: Phone signal
tips.accordion.signal.body: Coverage is spotty on the beach road. WiFi at Hacienda Café is the most reliable in town if you need to work or call home.
tips.accordion.roads.title: Getting around
tips.accordion.roads.body: The road from the highway is unpaved in sections — go slow after rain. A high-clearance car helps, but most guests make it fine in a regular sedan.
tips.accordion.groceries.title: Groceries & basics
tips.accordion.groceries.body: Hacienda Café has a small market with essentials. For a full shop, stop at Mega or Soriana in Zihuatanejo on your way in — your driver can help.
tips.accordion.respect.title: Local respect
tips.accordion.respect.body: La Saladita is a small fishing and surf community. Keep noise down at night, respect the lineup, and ask before photographing people or their property.
